drivers: Power Innovation commercialization beyond five projects and 2.6 GW (Socrates 556 MW, Apollo 490 MW, Aquila 520 MW, Socrates the Younger 340 MW, Neo 682 MW), counterparties and equipment slots
Contracted pipeline expansions on time and on budget (Transco SESE, NESE, Power Express, Delta Access, Shelby Trough Connector)
Leverage against the 3.5x to 4.0x range after Momentum and $7.3bn to $7.9bn of FY26 growth capex; rating agency treatment of the Blackstone JV
Hyperscaler credit and capital recovery within 10-year to 12.5-year PPA terms
Marketing (Sequent), hurricanes and gas prices as swing factors within the annual guidance
model:
Economic engine: Williams earns mostly fee-based, contracted revenue for moving, gathering, processing and storing natural gas. Transco, its regulated interstate pipeline, anchors the business, and Williams says it carries about one-third of US gas. Growth comes from fully contracted pipeline expansions and, since 2025, Power Innovation: on-site gas generation for data centers sold under long-term PPAs (FY25 10-K; 2Q26 10-Q).
Revenue map: transmission revenue = contracted firm capacity x reservation rate (regulated or negotiated), plus storage fees; gathering and processing = volumes x fees, with minimum volume commitments; Power Innovation revenue = MW x mostly fixed PPA price over 10 to 12.5 years; Gas & NGL Marketing (Sequent) margins are seasonal and weather-driven. Segments: Transmission, Power & Gulf (2Q26 Modified EBITDA $959mn), Northeast G&P ($540mn), West ($359mn), Marketing and Other. FY25 adjusted EBITDA was $7,750mn; the FY26 guide is $8.3bn to $8.5bn, and the 2025 to 2030 target is an 11%-plus CAGR.
Cost structure: O&M ($597mn in 2Q26), depreciation ($592mn in 2Q26) on long-lived pipe, G&A ($180mn), interest ($371mn in 2Q26) and cash taxes. Pipeline economics are capex-heavy up front, then low-cost and annuity-like.
Capital and funding: investment-grade (Baa2/BBB+/BBB). Debt was about $30.8bn gross at 30 June 2026, with leverage of 3.67x against a 3.5x to 4.0x target (about 3.9x expected at year-end with Momentum). FY26 growth capex is $7.3bn to $7.9bn. September 2026 notes were issued at 5.0% to 6.4%. Power Innovation is 49% funded by Blackstone with Apollo and KKR ($5.34bn for five projects, a 6.35% target return and a 10% promote, with a Williams buyout right from about 2033). Momentum Midstream ($5.5bn, closed 3 September 2026) was paid with about $3.5bn of cash and debt and about $2bn of stock. The dividend is $2.10 a year, with AFFO coverage of about 2.3x.
Sensitivities: rate cases and FERC policy on Transco; LNG and power-sector gas demand; Haynesville and Appalachia drilling and volumes; interest rates and spreads; hyperscaler credit and AI capex for Power Innovation; equipment (turbine, engine) supply; hurricanes and gas prices for Gulf and marketing.
Competitive position: Transco is the largest US gas pipeline and the main route into the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic power markets. Williams' integrated gas supply plus generation offer (Socrates was built in about 14 months from site handover) competes with other large pipeline groups (for example Kinder Morgan and Energy Transfer; general industry knowledge, not from filings) on pipe, and with developers and utilities on behind-the-meter power. Turbines are secured for the current backlog only.
What would break the model: (1) Power Innovation counterparties cut AI capex or end PPAs early without full capital recovery; (2) leverage persistently above 4x, risking the BBB+ rating; (3) adverse Transco rate or permitting outcomes that delay expansions; (4) equipment shortages that cap new power awards; (5) a structural fall in gas demand growth (LNG delays, power policy).
